name: Site Memory
description: A small website that becomes a personal mechanical atlas. Every visit, closer look and discovery leaves a remembered mark.

assets.credit: Original mechanical memory atlas · illustrative sample journey · Tampa Curated

compatibility: Modern Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge with SVG, ES modules, Web Animations and local storage. No WebGL or external runtime dependency.
Keyboard, mouse and touch use the same semantic exploration controls. The whole drawing fits narrow screens; Enlarge drawing exposes scrollable detail.
Reduced motion draws completed marks immediately and disables automatic replay. Hidden or offscreen studies suspend replay and line animation; settled drawings do not run a render loop.
Blocked, corrupt or full local storage leaves a usable session with JSON export and a clear warning. Accounts, analytics and server-side tracking are absent.
notes: Explore six rooms in an imaginary House of Small Discoveries. A dome, glasshouse, water wheel, printing press, lantern tower and drawing table gradually become a connected mechanical atlas. These miniature pages are the only activity recorded.

The first visit to a room adds an architectural object. Travel between rooms engraves a passage; revisiting strengthens it. Opening notes adds book marks, inspection adds gears, and completing a discovery leaves a pencil seal. Every event also has its own mark in the memory ribbon.

The order of first visits determines where the objects are placed. The journey seed, semantic event sequence and drawing settings determine all geometry; the engine does not use the current clock or random values while rendering.

Local persistence supports up to twelve journeys. Starting a new journey keeps earlier saved journeys available. Session-only mode stops writes without deleting earlier saves. Reset all history explicitly deletes only this experiment’s archive.

Replay scrubs the saved event sequence in either direction without recording new actions. Returning to the present restores the complete composition. The saved document retains the full journey while replay shows a temporary prefix.

Import validates versions, destinations, event types/order, timestamps, appearance and size. Failed imports preserve the current drawing. Concurrent edits in another tab block overwriting until the visitor resumes the saved version or begins a separate journey.
reuse: Serve the source ZIP over HTTP and open example.html. It includes the complete dependency-free demo and its settings. A visitor’s private journey is never silently added to the source package; export/import its JSON separately.
Use createMemory to accept visit, open, inspect and complete events, then renderJourney to turn the resulting document into deterministic SVG. Both are independent of the UI and browser storage.

Use mount(host, settings, report, integration) for the complete portable instrument. Supply destinations, an optional initial journey and a namespaced storage key. The returned record API accepts semantic events from your own website.
The README documents schemas, deterministic versioning, persistence, limits, privacy, replay and framework integration. Call dispose before removing the host.
